key_insight: The paper introduces accelerated second-order Lagrange-multiplier optimization schemes with variable splitting that maintain a dissipating pseudo-energy and converge to stationary points for non-convex problems.
engineering_relevance: These methods offer more stable and robust optimizers for difficult scientific computing tasks, including PDE-constrained learning, PINNs, and DeepONets.
method: Linear LM-based second-order flow for unconstrained non-convex optimization
Relaxed and adaptive updates to avoid multiplier degeneration and tune step size automatically
evidence_signal: The abstract reports extensive experiments on function optimization and PDE benchmarks, showing improved ability to escape local minima, high accuracy, and robustness to the initial learning rate in neural network training.
watch_item: Performance and stability may still depend on careful implementation of the second-order dynamics and adaptive rules, especially for large-scale or stiff problems.
paper_title: Several Accelerated and Stable Pseudo-Energy-Dissipative Lagrange Multiplier Methods based on Second-order Flow and Variable Splitting
